newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: INSTANT VIEW-Proton net 741.47 mln rgt.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW-Proton net 741.47 mln rgt.

text.p: Following is a selection of analysts' views on the financial results of Malaysian carmaker Perusahaan Otomobil Nasional Bhd (Proton). The company reported its net profit jumped to 741.47 million ringgit for the year ended March 31, 1997, against 355.88 million a year ago.
Its parent company, Hicom Holdings Bhd reported net earnings of 645.75 million ringgit against 297.37 million.
CORRINA CHEAH, AUTO ANALYST AT ING-BARINGS
"It's generally within market expectations or maybe slightly higher. Proton's (net profit) is about four percent higher than the market expectation.
"For Hicom, the (net profit) figure is about 10 percent higher -- the market was expecting 571.8 million (ringgit).
"So I'd say it looks very, very good. But it'll be better if we could have the breakdown on how much of the earnings came from the yen depreciation and how much from higher sales and cost savings."
MAZWIN ZAHID, ANALYST WITH CASPIAN SECURITIES
"Most people were expecting about a 1.0 billion ringgit pretax. Nonetheless, the results are generally within market expectations.
"I think poor sentiment still surrounds Proton. Even though it met market expectations, the price has not been moving.
"Our view on Proton is still a hold. Although its fundamentals are intact, they need another set of good results at the half-year, before confidence can be restored in the new leadership."
CHOO SWEE KEE, AUTO ANALYST AT VICKERS BALLAS
"Net profit is in line with expectations. We had forecast a profit of about 760 million ringgit. But it is above market consensus of 714 million.
"It's definitely a good set of results. How many companies can come out with such a high profit growth?
"It will be good for the stock. The stock has already started moving up today. It should go up a bit more on Monday."
AZIZAH AHMAD, AUTO ANALYST AT MBF NORTHERN SECURITIES:
"They were helped by the yen, especially in the second half.
"In the first half the yen was at 2.3 (ringgit per 100 yen). In the second half it was at 2.11, so even though the first half was very high the yen came down in the other six months.
(The ringgit closed in Kuala Lumpur trading on Friday at 2.1984/12 ringgit per 100 yen. Proton imports about 40 percent of its auto parts from Japan).
"Earnings-wise in the ongoing year it will depend on yen fluctuations.
"Our house view of the strengthening of the yen/ringgit is a temporary one. We are still bullish on Proton."
"I think their sales are going as we expected.
"The only worry is Tanjung Malim (new plant). I feel it's coming slower than expected.
